items.title: Briefed, bounded, measured delegation boundary
items.story: As a developer running Claude and Codex together, I want the handoff to be briefed, bounded and measured so that a run cannot stall silently, finish half the job, or ignore the rules I already wrote down.
acceptance_criteria: stage done refuses an empty diff, an out-of-scope change, a missing required test, or a failing per-task verify command
task stages are strictly sequential inside one story worktree, and task-level --parallel is refused
a decomposition recording prose where a runnable command belongs is refused
a --write delegation with no fresh recorded brief is denied by the hook, and the refusal names the command that fixes it
the generated brief carries the acceptance criteria, the write scope with its existing modules, and inlined design rules for user-facing work
forge codex status reports the write flag per job and flags a stalled one
forge doctor reports a required skill a runtime cannot load
forge next names the delegation step
items.outcome: Developers can now see the epic-to-story dependency hierarchy, start dependency-ready stories in separate worktrees, and execute each story's tasks sequentially through a protected, measured delegation boundary that refuses off-contract writes, overlapping workers, stale proof, and incomplete verification.

items.title: Legacy repo upgrade: one command, no residue
items.story: As an orchestrator upgrading a client repo vendored before the factory/ rename, I want one command to carry it onto the current harness, so that no stale copy of the gate surface survives and no story that was open at upgrade time becomes unclosable.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrading a repo that carries .agents/ leaves no .agents/ tree and a complete factory/ tree
Skill-evolution state (proposed, rejected) and client-added skills under .agents/skills/ survive at factory/skills/
A path under .agents/ with no counterpart in the vendored factory/ tree aborts the upgrade and is named; nothing under it is deleted
The upgrade output names every project-owned file still referencing .agents/, excluding archived evidence under .factory/history/
The migration modifies no project-owned file
Upgrading a repo already on factory/ behaves exactly as before
forge stage migrate --base <sha> records that base for each legacy stage it adopts, and refuses a base that does not resolve or is not an ancestor of HEAD
items.outcome: A repo vendored before the factory/ rename can now be carried onto the current harness in one command. `forge upgrade` detects the legacy .agents/ layout, carries the project's skills across, deletes the old tree only once every file left in it is provably the machinery being replaced, and otherwise refuses before writing anything — so a refusal leaves a clean repo you can repair and re-run. It then names the project-owned files still mentioning the retired path instead of editing them. `forge stage migrate --base <sha>` gives a story that was open at upgrade time a measurement origin, so it can still be closed. Four client repos were stranded with no migration path; decision 0016 promised them one and this is it.

items.title: The planning lock guards the harness's own source
items.story: As a maintainer dogfooding this harness on itself, I want the planning lock to treat factory/, docs/, constitution/ and harness/ as product IN THIS REPO so that a change to the gate machinery goes through a plan or a bounded window, the way every client's product code already does.
acceptance_criteria: A write under factory/ in the harness's own repo is refused without an approved plan with a recorded decomposition, or an open quickfix window.
The same paths stay writable during planning in a client repo, where they are vendored harness surface rather than the client's product.
A quickfix window in the harness repo claims the files it touches against its five-file budget, so the closed ledger entry reports the real scope instead of zero.
A test proves the two repo kinds are classified differently, so the distinction cannot silently regress.

items.title: Project and spec capture is complete or refused
items.story: As a developer opening a project I have not seen, I want the brief and its capability specs to be guaranteed complete, so that the board can show me what this product is instead of rendering blanks.
acceptance_criteria: record_signoff.py refuses when docs/product/BRIEF.md is missing a required heading or a required heading's body is empty, and names the heading.
forge spec confirm refuses a spec without an H1 title, Why, Behaviour, or Acceptance criteria, and names what is missing.
forge spec save still accepts an incomplete draft.
The brief template, its conventions doc and docs/product/BRIEF.md carry one canonical heading set including Target Outcome, and no heading in an already-written brief is renamed.
A brief or spec captured before this contract is reported by forge doctor and refused by nothing that already passed.
items.outcome: A brief or spec that is missing a required section is now refused at the gate that records it, instead of reaching sign-off half-written. Sign-off names every absent BRIEF heading, spec confirm requires Why, Behaviour and Acceptance criteria, and doctor reports legacy documents without blocking anyone. One shared parser answers 'does this document have this section' for all three, and it reads an example as an example: headings inside fenced blocks, HTML comments, raw blocks and container blocks no longer count as structure.

items.title: The roadmap hierarchy contract
items.story: As a planner, I want epics and stories to be refused unless they carry the fields the hierarchy needs, so that what the board draws is guaranteed to exist rather than hoped for.
acceptance_criteria: roadmap derive, import and add refuse an epic missing id, title, objective or resolvable source_refs, and a story missing narrative, acceptance criteria, skill, a known epic, or an explicit depends_on.
forge roadmap epic add creates an epic after sign-off, proven against a roadmap that has none.
The roadmap add --no-spec ad-hoc path still works and plan save still refuses to build its output.
mark_status, assign, link-spec and heal all still succeed against a roadmap captured before this contract.
unblocks, leverage and epic gating are derived from depends_on, and no route accepts them as authored input.
items.outcome: A story on the roadmap now has to say what it is: the three routes that author stories refuse one that omits its epic, narrative, acceptance criteria, skill or an explicit depends_on. Two new commands make that requirement satisfiable after sign-off — roadmap epic add creates an epic, set-epic points an existing story at one — and this repo's own roadmap was backfilled through them, so forge roadmap list finally prints its epic above the stories. Legacy roadmaps still load, still flip status and still heal; doctor reports their gaps without blocking, and no longer crashes on the broken state it exists to diagnose.

items.title: Plan and task contract
items.story: As a reviewer six weeks later, I want every approved plan to carry all nine sections and every task its own provenance, so that the argument for a change survives the person who made it.
acceptance_criteria: plan save refuses a plan missing any of the nine sections the planner prompt names, or carrying one with an empty body.
A recorded decomposition takes project, story, epic, plan path and plan digest from repository state, and a payload cannot override them.
Task verify_commands must be runnable, required_tests may be empty, and a task dependency may only name an earlier task.
build_waves is no longer authored by the decomposer prompt and its only reader is removed, while the schema still parses artifacts that carry it.
items.outcome: A plan is now refused unless it carries all nine sections the planner prompt mandates, checked with the shared parser instead of a substring that a fenced example could satisfy. A decomposition is bound to the plan it was built from: the recorder stamps project, story, epic, plan_file and the plan digest from trusted state and drops whatever an agent claimed, and stage start refuses when that plan has changed since — or when the binding cannot be verified at all. And build_waves stops being authored anywhere: prompts, the Codex agent contract, the doc and the scaffold check all let go of it together with its only reader, so ordering is derived from dependencies rather than written twice.

items.title: Present the hierarchy to engineers
items.story: As a new engineer, I want the default board screen to tell me what this project is, which stories I can start in parallel right now, and why the others are blocked, so that I can act without opening every card.
acceptance_criteria: Every epic, story and task on screen is explicitly labelled as such, and the drawer opens with a Project > Epic > Story breadcrumb.
/api/state and /api/story/<key> carry project identity, epic membership and derived relationships, and no mutating route exists.
The default view answers what the project is, what can start now, what each epic delivers, and why a story is blocked.
Blocked stories are described as blocked wherever the API reports blocked.
The bundled example passes the production validators and reads correctly at desktop, tablet and mobile widths.
items.outcome: Developers open the board and see the whole project: what it is, which stories can start right now and in how many worktrees, what each epic delivers, and why every blocked story is blocked — with epics, stories and tasks labelled as such and a Project > Epic > Story breadcrumb in the drawer. Blocked now reads as blocked on every surface instead of being folded into 'waiting', and a bundled example project ships that the production capture gates validate, so the board can be seen working before a repo has any work of its own.
